newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean industrial output off 3.7 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Chilean industrial output off 3.7 pct in March.

text.p: Industrial production tumbled 3.7 percent in March compared to March last year, and fell 0.9 percent in the first quarter, the National Statistics Institute reported.

The figures, closely in line with those issued by the private business group Sofofa on Monday, were the clearest sign yet of a mild slowdown in economic activity in the first months of the year in Chile.

Declines in production in March affected most major categories, including food production which was off 20.7 percent, clothing production, off 31 percent, and oil and coal products, off 19.8 percent, the Institute said.

A sharp drop in fishmeal production in March accounted largely for the decline in the food category and was responsible for up to a full percentage point of the overall monthly decline, institute officials told a news conference.
Nationwide sales of industrial products rose slightly in March, up 0.7 percent over the same month last year, and climbed 3.6 percent in the first quarter of the year, said the institute.
Sofofa's research division reported Monday that Chilean industrial production tumbled 3.7 percent in March and 0.3 percent in the first quarter of the year.
